name: NC-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+23 partisan lean makes it one of the most Democratic seats in North Carolina
Foushee holds an overwhelming financial edge: over $1 million raised and $2.4 million in outside support versus roughly $19,000 for Ganorkar
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 97 percent
No polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the forecast rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The D+23 lean of this Durham and Chapel Hill-area seat, Foushee's incumbency, and her lopsided fundraising and outside-spending advantage all point to a comfortable Democratic hold, and markets agree at roughly 97 percent. With no polling or ratings suggesting otherwise, the forecast stays at a wide Democratic margin.
model.watch: A surge of Republican outside spending or an unexpected scandal involving Foushee could narrow the margin, though the district's partisan lean makes an upset very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
North Carolina's 4th District, anchored by Durham and Chapel Hill, leans Democratic by 23 points, among the party's strongest seats in the state. Incumbent Valerie Foushee is seeking re-election after first winning the seat in 2022. She has raised more than $1 million and drawn about $2.4 million in outside support, while Republican Max Ganorkar has raised roughly $19,000. A Libertarian, Guy Meilleur, is also on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets put Democratic chances near 97 percent. The combination of the district's strong partisan lean, Foushee's incumbency, and her overwhelming financial advantage leaves little evidence of a competitive contest. The forecast expects Foushee to win by a wide margin, with the main uncertainty being turnout rather than the outcome.
